title.narrative: ROAS / IRAQ / Building Equitable and Inclusive Transformation (BEIT): Towards Decent Work and Affordable Housing in Iraq

description.narrative:
The proposed project aims to stimulate decent work opportunities for young women and men while addressing urgent need for affordable housing, especially for lower income and vulnerable people in Iraq. Action on job creation through affordable housing construction involves implementing specific strategies and initiatives. The project seeks to introduce a public works programme complementing support for addressing existing gaps within the Government and the private sector through Employment Intensive Investment Programme (EIIP) initiative. Furthermore, it aims to improve access to adequate and sustainable housing to create better living conditions for low-income and vulnerable populations; and build the capacities of the housing sector – including government actors and micro, small and medium enterprises, and civil society organizations – as a driver of economic growth.
The overall impact of the project is to stimulate decent work and improve living conditions, including for the most vulnerable, in Iraq. The objective is aligned with the EU Action Document (NDICI ASIA/2021/043-218) - Support to durable solutions for Iraq’s displaced populations: integration into the national labour market and national systems for education and social protection and its specific objective 1.1: promote an economic transformation that creates decent jobs and increases productive capacity.
The proposed actions will foster the following key elements while realizing the desired outcomes of the project:
Investment in affordable housing projects: Governments, both at the local and national levels, allocate funds for the development of affordable housing projects. These funds come from public budgets, private investments, or a combination of both. Allocating resources to affordable housing construction creates a demand for labour and materials, generating jobs in the construction sector.
Public-Private partnerships: Encourage public-private partnerships which allows collaboration between government agencies and private developers as well as MSMEs involved in the housing sector. These partnerships can help leverage private sector expertise and funding while ensuring that affordable housing remains a priority. Such collaborations can lead to more significant housing developments, translating into more and better job opportunities.
Diverse job opportunities: Affordable housing construction does not only create direct jobs but also generates indirect and induced employment opportunities in related industries like architecture, engineering, real estate, finance, and property management. Fostering a diverse job market can lead to a more sustainable and robust local economy.
Streamlining regulatory and legal frameworks permitting processes: Facilitating revisions to the legislative and policy framework that better enables affordable housing delivery including simplifying and expediting permitting processes can speed up construction timelines and reduce development costs. This can create a conducive environment for builders, attracting more investments and subsequently generating employment in the construction sector.
Building affordable housing technical competency for government officials: Capacity development of government actors, both at the national and governorate level, can support in building the skills and aptitude necessary for building an integrated affordable housing ecosystem, including developing effective policies and programs based on sound rules and regulations, administrative and compliance procedures, sound planning, and feasible finance mechanisms.
Updating the National Housing Policy: Updating the NHP can help build knowledge and evidence-based regarding Iraq’s current housing challenges, which will in turn support in building a concise and comprehensive road map to address these complex challenges.
Capacity building and skill development for local businesses: Investing in skills development for MSMEs and entrepreneurs in the housing and construction sector can improve the quality of labour available for affordable housing projects. By providing MSMEs with specialized skills and certifications, they become more efficient and effective to create employment opportunities and can contribute to the successful completion of housing developments integrating green and innovative practices.
Promoting small and women-owned businesses: Encouraging the participation of small and women-owned businesses in affordable housing projects create economic opportunities for underrepresented groups, especially women, who represent low rate of participation in the labour market.
